ancient

major

(adjective). Important, serious, or significant.

ex: All of her major plays have been translated into English.

historical

(adjective). Of or concerning history or past events.

ex: She specializes in historical novels set in 18th-century England.

suffer

(verb). Experience or be subjected to something bad or unpleasant

ex: I think he suffered a lot when his wife left him.

import

(verb). bring (goods or services) into a country from abroad for sale

ex: Japan's reluctance to import more cars

emission

(noun). The production and discharge of something,

ex: Bioluminescence is the emission of light from living organisms.

regulation

(noun). a rule or directive made and maintained by an authority.

ex: You should know the regulation of financial markets

moribund

(adjective). (of a person) at the point of death.

ex: How can the department be revived from its present moribund state?

innovation

(noun). the introduction of new things, ideas

ex: There's the latest innovations in computer technology

reputation

(noun). the beliefs or opinions that are generally held about someone or something.

ex: The company has a worldwide reputation for quality.

computerize

(verb). adapt (a system, device, etc.) to be operated by computer.

ex: he directed the finance department to computerize the entire pension system

management

(noun). the act of running and controlling a business

ex: The company has suffered from several years of bad management.

era

(noun). a period of time, usually in history, that is different from other periods

ex: They had worked for peace during the long era of conflict.

witness

(verb). A person who sees an event, typically a crime or accident, take place.

ex: Did anyone witness the attack?

elevation

(noun). the process of somebody getting a higher or more important rank

ex: This plan shows the front, side, and back elevations of the new supermarket.

fuel

(noun). Material such as coal, gas, or oil that is burned to produce heat or power

ex: Wood, coal, oil, petrol, and gas are all different kinds of fuel.

toxic

(adjective). oisonous.

ex: He's in a toxic relationship

climate

(noun). the weather conditions prevailing in an area in general or over a long period.

ex: there's a climate of economic uncertainty

pollute

(verb). to add dirty or harmful substances to land, air, water, etc. so that it is no longer pleasant or safe to use

ex: The pesticides used on many farms are polluting the water supply.

adventurous

(adjective). Willing to take risks or to try out new methods, ideas, or experiences.

ex: He's an adventurous traveler

bunch

(noun). a number of things

ex: There's a bunch of grapes on the table

convertible

(adjective). Able to be changed in form, function, or character

ex: It's a living room that is miraculously convertible into a bedroom

reasonable

(adjective). Having sound judgement;

ex: If you tell him what happened, I'm sure he'll understand - he's a reasonable man.

interchangeable

(adjective). (of two things) able to be interchanged.

ex: The terms "drinking problem" and "alcohol abuse" are often interchangeable.

productivity

(noun). The state or quality of being productive.

ex: Studies show that if a working environment is pleasant, productivity increases.

manpower

(noun). The number of people working or available for work or service.

ex: the police had only limited manpower

integrate

(verb). Combine (one thing) with another to form a whole.

ex: The idea with young children is to integrate learning with play.

artful

(adjective). Clever or skilful, especially in a crafty or cunning way.

ex: That's an artful photograph of a striking woman

joint venture

(noun). a business or business activity that two or more people or companies work on together

ex: The website was a joint venture between him and his partner.

unify

(verb). to join people, things, parts of a country

ex: If the new leader does manage to unify his warring party it will be quite an achievement.

captive

(noun). A person who has been taken prisoner or an animal that has been confined.

ex: When the town was recaptured, we found soldiers who had been captives for several years.

badge

(noun). a small piece of metal or plastic to show that they belong to an organization, support something, have achieved something

ex: Everyone at the conference wore a badge with their name on .

consolidation

(noun). the action or process of making something stronger or more solid.

ex: Think of a consolidation of data within an enterprise

marque

(noun). A make of car, as distinct from a specific model.

ex: think of marques such as Bentley, Ferrari, or Porsche

injection

(noun). An instance of injecting or being injected.

ex: Sometimes a polio vaccine is given by injection.

emphasis

(noun). Special importance, value, or prominence

ex: Schools here put/place/lay great emphasis on written work and grammar.

sections.title: Passage 3: Elephant Communication
sections.html:
hammer

(noun). a tool with a heavy metal head mounted at right angles at the end of a handle, used for jobs such as breaking things and driving in nails

ex: She hit her thumb with the hammer.

preposition

(noun). a word governing, and usually preceding, a noun or pronoun and expressing a relation to another word or element in the clause

ex: Some prepositions consist of more than one word, such as 'out of'.

proportionally

(adverb). in a way that increases or decreases in size, amount or degree according to changes in something else

ex: health problems increased proportionally to the number of hours worked

mammal

(noun). A warm-blooded vertebrate animal

ex: Humans, dogs, elephants, and dolphins are all mammals, but birds, fish, and crocodiles are not.

vibrational

(adjective). of vibration

ex: The vibrational specific heat in all our examples is large.

signal

(noun). A gesture, action, or sound that is used to convey information or instructions,

ex: When she gave (them) the signal, they all cheered.

massive

(adjective). Large and heavy or solid.

ex: They have a massive house.

frequency

(noun). The rate at which something occurs over a particular period of time

ex: Complaints about the frequency of buses rose in the last year.

takeoff

(noun). The action of becoming airborne.

ex: The plane accelerated down the runway for takeoff

frame

(noun). A rigid structure that surrounds something such as a picture, door

ex: It's a picture frame

transmit

(verb). to send an electronic signal, radio or television broadcast, etc.

ex: The information is transmitted electronically to the central computer.

inner

(adjective). inside; towards or close to the centre of a place

ex: Leading off the main hall is a series of small inner rooms.

jet

(verb). Spurt out in jets

ex: blood jetted from his nostrils

pad

(noun). A thick piece of soft material, typically used to protect or shape something

ex: Soccer players often wear shin pads to protect their legs.

fatty

(adjective). containing a large amount of fat.

ex: Dont eat fatty foods

bone

(noun). Any of the pieces of hard whitish tissue making up the skeleton

ex: The child was so thin that you could see her bones.

sinus

(adjective). relating to or denoting the sinoatrial node of the heart or its function as a pacemaker.

ex: My sinuses are all plugged from crying.

cavity

(noun). an empty space within a solid object, in particular the human body.

ex: Some birds nest in tree cavities

skull

(noun). a framework of bone or cartilage enclosing the brain of a vertebrate; the skeleton of a person's or animal's head.

ex: he broke his collar bone and fractured his skull

riddle

(noun). A question or statement intentionally phrased so as to require ingenuity

ex: Scientists may have solved the riddle of Saturn's rings.

function

(verb). work or operate in a proper or particular way.

ex: her liver is functioning normally

resonate

(verb). to make a deep, clear sound that continues for a long time

ex: The noise of the bell resonated through the building.

chamber

(noun). A large room used for formal or public events.

ex: Meetings of the council are held in the council chamber.

trunk

(noun). The main woody stem of a tree

ex: The statue shows the head, trunk, and arms of an old man.

infrasonic

(adjective). Relating to or denoting sound waves with a frequency below the lower limit of human audibility.

ex: At Amboseli, several different infrasonic calls have been identified.

postdoctoral

(adjective). connected with advanced research or study that is done after a PhD has been completed

ex: She was a postdoctoral fellow at Princeton University and at the University of Washington in Seattle

sense

(noun). A faculty by which the body perceives an external stimulus

ex: I have no sense whatever of dramatic action, and could make only random guesses

detect

(verb). Discover or identify the presence or existence of.

ex: The inquisitors at once began to detect errors

pachyderm

(noun). a very large mammal with thick skin, especially an elephant, rhinoceros, or hippopotamus

ex: Their contention is the stage is not strong enough to have the pachyderm onstage

nerve

(noun). any of the long threads that carry messages between the brain and parts of the body, enabling you to move, feel pain, etc.

ex: Her nerve began to frazzle.

ending

(noun). An end or final part of something, especially a period of time, an activity, or a book or movie.

ex: They reached the ending of the Cold War

ecology

(noun). the branch of biology that deals with the relations of organisms

ex: The ecology movement seems particularly adept in its innovative approach to venues.

geophysics

(noun). The physics of the earth

ex: It was used for physical oceanography, marine geophysics and marine biology including krill and fish

neurophysiology

(noun). The physiology of the nervous system.

ex: Neurophysiology and genetic research will, without doubt, have profound social impacts.

boundless

(adjective). without limits

ex: enthusiasts who devote boundless energy to their hobby

unpredictable

(adjective). cannot be predicted

ex: Darian had a quick wit that was as unpredictable as his actions.

interface

(noun). A point where two systems, subjects, organizations, etc. meet and interact.

ex: The software has a user interface that's easy to operate.

seismic

(noun). relating to earthquakes or other vibrations of the earth and its crust.

ex: after a few days of seismic activity the volcanic eruption started

exist

(verb). to be present in a place or situation

ex: She believes that ghosts really do exist.

extensively

(adverb). In a way that covers or affects a large area.

ex: Tobacco is very extensively cultivated in the vicinity

scorpion

(noun). a small creature similar to an insect that lives in hot, dry areas of the world and has a long body and a curved tail with a poisonous sting

ex: The scorpion and the centipede are both common.

insect

(noun). Small animal that has six legs and generally one or two pairs of wings

ex: A boot came down on the angry insect before it could reach her.

spider

(noun). a small creature with eight thin legs that catches insects in a web

ex: A spider landed on her pillow and she screamed

vertebrate

(noun). an animal that has a spine

ex: Tadpoles are aquatic vertebrates

rat

(noun). a small animal with a long tail, that looks like a large mouse, usually considered a pest

ex: Rat did kill baby pigeons.

auditory

(adjective). Relating to the sense of hearing.

ex: The patient has damage to the auditory nerve

planthopper

(noun). a small, widely distributed plant-sucking bug that leaps when disturbed. Some species are pests of rice and sugar cane

ex: When the spraying stopped, the spiders ate the planthoppers

stem

(noun). The main body or stalk of a plant or shrub,

ex: She twisted the stem of her glass

existence

(noun). The fact or state of living or having objective reality.

ex: It wasn't normal for them to acknowledge her existence, let alone address her

press

(noun). A device for applying pressure to something in order to flatten or shape it

ex: To start the machine, just give this button a press.

exhibit

(verb). Publicly display (a work of art or item of interest) in an art gallery

ex: The authorities began to exhibit something of their old spirit

freeze

(verb). turn or be turned into ice or another solid as a result of extreme cold.

ex: We'll freeze to death

fascinating

(adjective). Extremely interesting

ex: It was a bewildering and fascinating place.

mate

(verb). to have sex in order to produce young (animals)

ex: a male bird sings to court a mate

herd

(noun). a group of animals of the same type that live and feed together

ex: It's a herd of elephants

predator

(noun). An animal that naturally preys on others.

ex: he population of rabbits is controlled by natural predators.

capacity

(noun). A specified role or position.

ex: Energy is the capacity for doing work

survival

(noun). the act or fact of living or continuing longer than another person or thing

ex: His own survival was more important.

wild

(adjective). a place being uninhabited, uncultivated, or inhospitable.

ex: Any time a wild animal isn't afraid of you, there is probably something wrong

reproductive

(adjective). Relating to or effecting reproduction.

ex: Look at the female reproductive system

biology

(noun). the scientific study of the natural processes of living things

ex: The book deals with the reproductive biology of the buffalo.

vast

(adjective). extremely large

ex: He was so tall there was a vast difference in their height

outcome

(noun). The way a thing turns out; a consequence # income (n), salary

ex: This was the only outcome we could allow.

adopt

(verb). Take on or assume (an attitude or position)

ex: He was so tall there was a vast difference in their height

alert

(noun). the state of being watchful for possible danger.

ex: He's always been so alert and in control.

vulnerable

(adjective). Exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally

ex: Children are the most vulnerable members of society

susceptible

(adjective). easily influenced by feelings and emotions

ex: Children are much more susceptible than adults

hyena

(noun). a wild animal from Africa and Asia that looks like a dog, hunts in groups, and makes a sound similar to a human laugh

ex: The striped hyena is scattered over the country sparsely

clump

(noun). A compacted mass or lump of something.

ex: Its lofty site is now marked by a clump of trees.

attitude

(noun). A settled way of thinking or feeling about something

ex: She was tired of fighting, tired of his attitude, tired of everything.

warble

(verb). sing softly and with a succession of constantly changing notes.

ex: Verb Birds were warbling in the trees.

tense

(verb). become tense, typically through anxiety or nervousness.

ex: Her body tensed up.

rumble

(verb). to make a long deep sound or series of sounds

ex: Please excuse my stomach rumbling - I haven't eaten all day.

aggressively

(adverb). in an angry and violent way

ex: Small children often behave aggressively.

flee

(verb). Run away from a place or situation of danger.

ex: She fled (from) the room in tears.

clear-cut

(adjective). easy to perceive or understand

ex: Medicine is not clear-cut; there are many gray areas

wildlife

(noun). Wild animals collectively; the native fauna (and sometimes flora) of a region.

ex: The wildlife out here depends on the water hole

mystical

(adjective). having spiritual powers or qualities that are difficult to understand or to explain

ex: That's a geometric figure of mystical significance

realm

(noun). A kingdom.

ex: I'll take what I want from your realm, Watcher.

colleague

(noun). A person with whom one works in a profession or business.

ex: The businessman wanted to be separated from his noisy colleague.

revelation

(noun). A surprising and previously unknown fact that has been disclosed to others.

ex: The book includes many shocking revelations about the mayor's personal life.

stunning

(adjective). extremely attractive or impressive (ấn tượng)

ex: He was the most stunning man she'd ever seen despite his crooked nose.

infrasound

(noun). Sound waves with frequencies below the lower limit of human audibility.

ex: Those are infrasound generators

cranial

(adjective). Relating to the skull or cranium.

ex: The skull is high, with -the facial and cranial portions approximately equal.

canal

(noun). a long straight passage dug in the ground and filled with water for boats and ships to travel along; a smaller passage used for carrying water to fields, crops, etc.

ex: THat's the ear canal

versatile

(adjective). able to do many different things

ex: Galen was one of the most versatile and accomplished writers of his age

appendage

(noun). a smaller or less important part of something larger

ex: they treat Scotland as a mere appendage of England

savanna

(noun). a wide flat open area of land, especially in Africa, that is covered with grass but has few trees

ex: In the savannas are gigantic baobab trees.
